nodes.label:
Notice a Frustration
Signal
nodes.title: Notice a Frustration Signal
nodes.info: Folded arms, silence, muttering, or redoing the same failed step without changing anything -- the early signs handling frustration teaches a mentor to watch for.

nodes.label:
What
Triggered It?
nodes.title: What Triggered It?
nodes.info: The right tool depends on whether this is a single hard moment, a pattern building across weeks, or a task that just ended in a concrete failure.

nodes.label:
Use Encouragement
Language
nodes.title: Use Encouragement Language
nodes.info: Name the difficulty honestly and redirect toward the specific next action, without dismissing the struggle as trivial.

nodes.label:
Apply Persistence
Coaching
nodes.title: Apply Persistence Coaching
nodes.info: Notice the pattern out loud and reopen the abandoned task deliberately, in a low-stakes way, rather than leaving it to chance.

nodes.label:
Reframe as a
Learning Tool
nodes.title: Reframe as a Learning Tool
nodes.info: Treat the error or wrong result as data that narrows down the next attempt, not as a verdict on the student's ability.

nodes.label:
Student Re-Engages
With the Task
nodes.title: Student Re-Engages With the Task
nodes.info: Every path aims at the same outcome: the student returns to the problem instead of quietly giving up on it.
